issue.title: Decide the two sase-core wheel-size tradeoffs measured by sase-13t.2: macOS arm64-only (-20.2%/release) and opt-level=s (-31.3% wheel, +16-24% Rust time)
issue.description:
Epic sase-13t phase `sase-13t.2` measured every link-time option against the real `sase_core_rs` extension module and, per the plan's explicit "report, do not decide" rule, **landed nothing**. Two decisions are the user's to make and are the only unspent wheel-size savings left. All measurement work is already done; a worker applies the decision, it does not re-measure.

## Decision 1 — macOS: `universal2` or `arm64`-only?

Measured on the live 0.34.67 universal2 wheel (29,358,870 B): x86_64 slice 35,274,104 B raw / 14,880,891 B deflated; arm64 slice 30,249,280 B raw / 13,543,644 B deflated.

- arm64-only wheel: ~13.58 MB, saving **~15.78 MB per release** = 53.8% of the macOS wheel and **20.2% of the 78.33 MB release**.
- Cost: **drops Intel Mac support.** That is a product support-matrix call, which is why the phase left the wheel `universal2`.
- Change if accepted: the `macos` job's `target: universal2-apple-darwin` in `sase-core` `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`, plus the `universal2.whl` entry in the workflow-level `EXPECTED_DIST_SUFFIXES` list (the publish gate compares `dist/` to it one-to-one and will fail before upload if only one side is changed).

## Decision 2 — `[profile.release]` `opt-level`?

Baseline (thin LTO, opt-level 3): `.so` 38,531,072 B, wheel 16,212,682 B. Rust kernel timings are rotated min-of-rounds A/B plus the 30-scenario `tests/perf` benches.

| variant | wheel | delta | Rust kernel time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| base | 16,212,682 | — | 1.00 |
| `opt-level = 2` | 15,487,548 | -4.5% | query kernels ~+5-10%, parse -3..+1% |
| `opt-level = "s"` | 11,144,887 | **-31.3%** | **+16-24% on every kernel** |
| `opt-level = "z"` | 9,940,431 | -38.7% | +56-61% on every kernel |
| `lto = "fat"` | 16,165,827 | -0.3% | 0.88-0.99 (slightly faster) |

`opt-level = "s"` is the interesting one: ~24 MB saved per release across the 4 binary wheels, for query evaluate 180 -> 209 us at 1000 specs and parse of a 118 KB file 5.7 -> 6.6 ms. `sase-core` is a performance-sensitive core library, so this is a real tradeoff, not free.

Also measured and **not** recommended: putting only the gateway/HTTP stack at `z` gives -4.9% wheel bytes at 0% runtime cost, but needs ~93 versioned `[profile.release.package."name@ver"]` overrides (hyper/http/socket2/base64 each ship two versions, so bare names are ambiguous) that go stale on every dependency bump. `lto = "fat"` shrinks the `.so` 4.5% but only 0.3% of the wheel, because compression absorbs it. Do **not** set `panic = "abort"`: PyO3 needs unwinding to surface Python exceptions.

## Context for whether this is still worth doing

Storage pressure is no longer acute: after the epic's retention run and the cadence change the project sits at 2.27 GB of its 10 GiB limit with ~108 releases of runway at 1 release/day. These savings extend that runway; they are not needed to keep publishing working. Declining both and closing this bead is a legitimate outcome — record the decision either way so the measurements are not re-run.

Full measurement detail, method, and the symbol-level byte breakdown are in note #1 on bead `sase-13t.2`.

task_type_fields.proposal: Take the user's decision on the two measured wheel-size tradeoffs and apply it: (a) build the macOS wheel arm64-only instead of universal2 (~15.78 MB/release, 20.2% of a release; costs Intel Mac support) by changing the macos job target and the matching EXPECTED_DIST_SUFFIXES entry in sase-core .github/workflows/release-plz.yml together; and/or (b) set opt-level = "s" in [profile.release] of the sase-core workspace Cargo.toml (-31.3% wheel bytes for +16-24% Rust kernel time). Declining both and recording that decision is an acceptable outcome. No re-measurement is needed; sase-13t.2 note #1 holds the full data.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-13t's plan explicitly scoped phase sase-13t.2 to 'report, do not decide': it required the macOS slice saving to be quantified and surfaced as a question rather than applied, and forbade landing an opt-level change that shrinks the artifact at the cost of measurable runtime. Both are product/performance calls that belong to the user, not to an agent, so the phase landed nothing and filed them as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP decisions.
